interpretation_summary: The three artifacts are broadly aligned on one narrow claim: for task004, boundary scanning belongs to the hosting-capacity assessment family, while single-point mismatch belongs to operating-point analysis and should not substitute for boundary evaluation. The literature positioning is conservative (`variant`), and the upgrade artifact already narrows the valid claim to static boundary judgment within the current scan envelope and control strategy. This is a defensible literature-aligned refinement, not evidence of a strongly novel method or broadly new theory.

agreement_with_rule_baseline.summary: I agree with the baseline upgrade if it is interpreted as a guarded cognition refinement rather than a strong novelty claim.
details: The literature alignment explicitly places the route as `variant`, which correctly limits novelty.
The explanation alignment supports the category distinction between boundary assessment and single-point operation analysis.
The upgrade's `claim_adjustment` is appropriately conservative and should remain attached to any downstream reporting.

new_insights: The strongest cross-artifact signal is not novelty, but category hygiene: the main contribution is preventing a problem-type mix-up between conditioned boundary assessment and single-point operating evaluation.

The support quality is uneven: some evidence is direct excerpt support, but some items rely on card-tag fallback or low-strength manual summary, so the apparent count of excerpts should not be read as uniformly strong evidence.
Current evidence better supports a boundary-of-validity clarification than a new mechanism claim.
overclaim_warnings: Do not treat keyword or topic overlap with hosting-capacity papers as proof that the local method is method-equivalent to those papers.
Do not promote `variant` positioning into a claim of substantial methodological novelty.
Do not use the current artifacts to claim general hosting-capacity conclusions beyond the present scan envelope, control strategy, and static setting.
Do not interpret the explanation-alignment support count as all-direct, full-text-confirmed literature support; some support is fallback-based or low-strength.
missing_evidence: Seed literature coverage is still limited to a small set of papers and family-level mapping; this is weak for stronger novelty positioning.
Full-text or finer-grained semantic matching is missing; the explanation artifact itself notes that full-text semantic matching has not been done.
Several review-derived explanation points remain `unclear`, which weakens confidence in broader literature-backed interpretation.
There is no evidence here for transfer to other operating conditions, other control policies, dynamic/time-series settings, or broader system classes.

next_steps: Retain the cognition upgrade as a bounded clarification of problem type and claim boundary.
Preserve the current claim adjustment verbatim in downstream cognition/report objects.
Expand literature coverage beyond the current seed set before making any stronger novelty statement.
Add fuller excerpt/full-text alignment, especially for the review paper and any papers representing alternative hosting-capacity method families.
If possible, test whether the boundary-vs-single-point distinction still holds under additional control strategies or non-static settings.
